books.section: Topic 3.13 Continuity and Change in Period 3

primary_sources: Alexander Hamilton, Report on Manufactures, December 5, 1791

stimulus.text:
Alexander Hamilton, Report on Manufactures, December 5, 1791:

“Not only the wealth; but the independence and security of a Country, appear to be materially connected with the prosperity of manufactures. Every nation, with a view to those great objects, ought to endeavour to possess within itself all the essentials of national supply. These comprise the means of Subsistence habitation clothing and defence.”
stimulus.source_note: Alexander Hamilton, Report on Manufactures, December 5, 1791. Founders Online, National Archives. Public domain.

source: original; stimulus quoted from Alexander Hamilton, Report on Manufactures, December 5, 1791, public domain.
stem: According to Hamilton, why should the United States encourage manufactures?

options.text: To make the United States depend on Britain for supplies.
options.misconception: Hamilton wanted the opposite: independence from foreign nations for supplies.

options.text: To end all farming in the United States.
options.misconception: Hamilton never calls for ending farming; he calls for adding manufactures.

options.text: To lower every tax in the country to zero.
options.misconception: Hamilton says nothing about taxes in this passage.

options.text: Manufactures would bring wealth, independence, and security.

rationales.A: Hamilton wanted the opposite: independence from foreign nations for supplies.
rationales.B: Hamilton never calls for ending farming; he calls for adding manufactures.
rationales.C: Hamilton says nothing about taxes in this passage.
rationales.D: Hamilton ties manufactures to wealth, independence, and security, and to supplying the nation itself.
rationales.general:
1. Read Hamilton's sentence: wealth, independence, and security all rest on manufactures.
2. He wants the nation to supply itself with subsistence, clothing, and defence.
3. That means making goods at home instead of depending on foreign nations.
4. So manufactures, for Hamilton, were a matter of national safety, not only of money.
Remember: when a writer lists three gains, all three belong in the answer.
